newsitem.title: UK: Romania to revise 1997 budget in July - minister.
newsitem.headline: Romania to revise 1997 budget in July - minister.

text.p: Romania will revise the 1997 state budget in July to include recent changes in macro-economic indicators and new fiscal rules, Finance Minster Mircea Ciumara said on Thursday.

"I don't see the need to change the spending structure. But the (revised) budget will include changes in revenues," Ciumara told a news conference ahead of the launching of the Romania's first mark-denominated Eurobond, estimated at about 700 million marks.
"We are presenting right now to parliament laws to change the taxation system...we will also keep in mind the effect of price liberalisation," he added.

Last month Romania adopted an austerity budget -- agreed with international lenders -- seeking to cut the consolidated budget deficit to 4.5 percent of the gross domestic product in 1997 from about 5.8 percent in 1996.
The consolidated budget includes state budget, local government budgets, social security budget and various extra-budgetary funds.
The new centrist coalition government, which ousted leftists in 1996 elections, had embarked on a shock-therapy programme to reshape the economy.

Last month, the International Monetary Fund approved $430 million in credits to back up Romania's reforms. The World Bank is also expected to approve a package of loans totalling $625 million next week.
"Now we have the financing ensured and we can be more sure on further developments," Ciumara said.
The bulk of the 1997 budget gap will be financed though external credits, with the rest funded by borrowing from the domestic market.

The government has so far implemented tough monetary policies ahead of freeing fuel, energy and food prices, a move which pushed monthly inflation to 30.7 percent in March before sliding to 6.9 percent last month.

Under the 1997 budget, year-on-year inflation was put at 90 percent, but the impact of price liberalisation was higher than expected, with consumer prices rising by 89.5 percent in April from December 1996.
Romanian officials have recently revised upward their estimates putting the year-on-year inflation to about 110 to 120 percent. That figure is likely to be included in the revised budget.
The government also pledged to ease income and profit taxes -- now at up to 60 percent and 45 percent respectively -- in the second half of this year.
Latest data put the state budget gap at 1.98 trillion lei in the first quarter this year, or 16 percent of the forecast, reflecting a cautious spending policy.

Ciumara also said he was planning to "decentralise" the activity of his ministry while increasing the role of local administrations" but he gave no further details. -- Mirela Eremia, London Newsroom 171 5426414
